basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 47:4 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 275. Quaeritur quomodo in terra Aegypti pascua pecoribus inveniri potuerunt, cum'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 275. Quaeritur quomodo in terra Aegypti pascua pecoribus inveniri potuerunt, cum ea terra pluviis non irrigatur; et fratres Joseph ideo terram Chanaan reliquisse [se] dicunt, quod herbas gregibus suis non invenissent (Gen. XLVII, 4)?-- Resp. Perhibetur ab eis qui loca sciunt, in multis Aegypti paludibus potuisse pascua non deesse, etiam cum fames esset frumentorum, quae solent Nili fluminis inundatione provenire. Magis enim dicuntur paludes illae feraces [ Ms., feracius] pascua gignere, quando aqua Nili minus excrescit.
